name: Transaction value — the two conditions under which the price IS the value
definition: Section 15(1) does not say the value is the price. It says the value is the transaction value, defines the transaction value as the price actually paid or payable for the said supply, and then attaches TWO conditions to the whole statement: the supplier and the recipient are not related, AND the price is the sole consideration for the supply. Both must hold. Where either fails, s.15(1) does not produce a value at all and s.15(4) sends the supply to the prescribed Rules. The transaction value so found is a STARTING amount, not the final one — s.15(2) then adds and s.15(3) then subtracts.
why_it_exists: Section 9(1) levies central tax 'on the value determined under section 15'. Section 15(1) is therefore the first fork in every taxable supply: either the invoice price is admissible as the base, or it is not and a Rule must compute one. Stating the two conditions separately is the point — an engine that checks only relatedness will value a barter at its cash leg, and an engine that checks only sole-consideration will value a transfer to a subsidiary at whatever the group chose to charge.
inputs: the price actually paid or payable for the said supply
whether the supplier and the recipient of the supply are related (GST-VAL-RELATED-DISTINCT)
whether the price is the sole consideration for the supply
outputs: CONDITION 1 — not related: satisfied, failed, or unknown
CONDITION 2 — price is the sole consideration: satisfied, failed, or unknown
where BOTH are satisfied: the transaction value, before the s.15(2) additions and the s.15(3) exclusions
where EITHER fails: no value under s.15(1), and a referral to GST-VAL-CASCADE
preconditions: the transaction is a supply under s.7 (GST-SUPPLY-SCOPE)
a price actually paid or payable for the said supply is identified — not a list price, not an estimate
exceptions: CONDITION 1 fails — supplier and recipient are related within the s.15 Explanation: s.15(1) does not apply, rule 28 governs (GST-VAL-RELATED-DISTINCT)
CONDITION 2 fails — consideration not wholly in money: s.15(1) does not apply, rule 27 governs (GST-VAL-NON-MONEY)
s.15(5) — for supplies notified by the Government the prescribed manner applies notwithstanding s.15(1), so both conditions being satisfied does not save the transaction value (GST-VAL-CASCADE)
UNKNOWN — notifications made under the Act and the Rules are not held locally. A notification can narrow or displace a limb without the section or rule text changing.
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
common_mistakes: reading s.15(1) as 'the value is the invoice price' and stopping there — the conditions and the s.15(2) additions are part of the same sentence and the same section
testing only relatedness and treating a part-exchange or barter as if the cash leg were the whole price — CONDITION 2 is independent
treating the transaction value as the final taxable value — it is the base to which s.15(2) adds
reading 'price actually paid or payable' as 'price actually received' — payable is enough, so an unpaid invoice still carries its value
assuming the two conditions are alternatives — the statute joins them with 'and'
legal_references: CGST Act 2017, s.15(1) — transaction value and its two conditions
CGST Act 2017, s.9(1) — the levy is on the value determined under section 15
CGST Act 2017, s.15(4) — where s.15(1) cannot determine the value
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — s.15(1) fixes a statutory tax base. It is not the accounting measurement of revenue, and the two amounts can legitimately differ on the same transaction
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the tax invoice or contract stating the price actually paid or payable
evidence of the relationship, or its absence, between supplier and recipient
evidence that nothing beyond the money price moved from recipient to supplier — no goods taken in exchange, no service rendered back, no obligation discharged
confidence_factors: weak when only the invoice is held — neither condition is visible on the face of an invoice
zero when the relationship between the parties is unknown, because s.15(1) is conditional on it and an unknown condition is not a satisfied one
zero when a non-money element of the consideration is suspected but not quantified
strong only when both conditions are separately evidenced, not inferred from the invoice
validation_checks: CONDITION 1 is recorded as an explicit determination, never assumed from the absence of contrary evidence
CONDITION 2 is recorded as an explicit determination, never assumed from the presence of a money price
where either condition is unknown, the value is NOT taken from s.15(1)
the amount produced here is labelled as the transaction value before s.15(2) and s.15(3), not as the taxable value
examples: an arm's-length cash sale between two unconnected registered persons at an agreed price — both conditions satisfied, the transaction value is that price
counterexamples: goods sold to a subsidiary at an agreed cash price — CONDITION 2 is satisfied but CONDITION 1 fails, so s.15(1) does not apply
a new phone supplied for money plus an old phone taken in exchange — CONDITION 1 may be satisfied but CONDITION 2 fails, so s.15(1) does not apply and rule 27 governs

evidence.quote: The value of a supply of goods or services or both shall be the transaction value, which is the price actually paid or payable for the said supply of goods or services or both where the supplier and the recipient of the supply are not related and the price is the sole consideration for the supply.
on the value determined under section 15
Where the value of the supply of goods or services or both cannot be determined under sub-section (1), the same shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed.
